title: Rank clusters containing a closed-kind entry retire from the ranking
action: Evolving Gate A pick (freshness): the top-ranked feedback cluster is a P1 that was fixed and closed weeks-to-days ago — closed rows exist but under different titles, so nothing links them and the dead item keeps topping the agenda. Fix in feedback.rs (rank/cluster path — KIND_ALIASES maps backlog-closed to normalized kind 'closed'): (1) after clustering, any cluster containing at least one entry whose normalized kind is 'closed' is EXCLUDED from the ranked list; (2) excluded clusters are reported in a separate `retired` array in the --json payload (representative title + entry count) so nothing silently vanishes — the text render mentions the retired count in one line; (3) ranking arithmetic for surviving clusters is byte-identical. The retire CONVENTION rides the existing normalized-title grouping: appending a backlog-closed row bearing the SAME title as the target cluster makes them cluster together and tombstones it — no new linkage field, append-only log untouched. TDD red-first: fixture backlog with a friction row + a closed row sharing a normalized title -> cluster absent from ranked output, present in retired; a friction-only cluster ranks exactly as before (pin one existing rank tuple); a closed-only row also lands in retired, never ranked. Keep every existing feedback test green.

truths: a cluster with any closed-kind entry never appears in the ranked list and always appears in retired
surviving clusters rank byte-identical to today
the json payload names retired clusters so nothing silently vanishes

artifacts.substantive: retire filter plus tests, no TODO stubs

trace.outcome: clusters with any closed-kind entry leave the ranking into a retired array; surviving ranks byte-identical; retire convention = append-only same-title backlog-closed row
deviations: rank --json payload shape changed from bare array to {ranked, retired} - an array cannot carry the named sibling; consumers indexing the bare array must move to .ranked
